attempts.entry_title: Prefrontal ensembles in platform-mediated avoidance (Gabriel et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The dandiset holds no calcium imaging, so the findings were tested on the authors' analysed data on Zenodo. There, avoidance learning held, as did better decoding of trial outcome in shocked mice and the best fit of a hybrid Rescorla-Wagner model, the last two under assumed readings of the methods. The day 2 rise in mixed-selective prefrontal neurons did not reproduce: shocked mice had fewer than controls, where the paper reports 51% against 25%, and the paper does not describe how it counts a mixed cell. Decoding did not peak just before the shock. Cells tracked across days and the latent-trajectory analyses could not be tested, as no registration is deposited and CILDS runs only in MATLAB.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gabriel, Gupta, Sanchez-Fuentes, Zeidler, Wilke and DeNardo (2025) on dandiset 001887 and on the paper's Zenodo record of analyzed datasets. The dandiset holds trial tables and behaviour videos for 16 mice and no calcium imaging; the Zenodo record holds the Minian traces and BehaviorDEPOT labels of the 30 imaged sessions. The notebook links the two, checks the clocks, and tests the behaviour, ROC encoding, platform-event, decoding and Rescorla-Wagner claims.

disagreements.reason: The criterion as written is met: under the assumed reading (C1 N1, clock windows) shocked mice are higher with Sidak p < 0.05 in the pre-shock and shock epochs in all three cohorts (cell 72). The shuffled-label control is not part of the criterion, and the paper has none; using it to change the outcome replaces the written criterion with a new one, and its result belongs in the notes as a caveat. The control answers my round-2 concern in the authors' favour (with shuffled labels the groups do not differ, p = 0.455; successes do not predict the shuffled value, r = 0.16, p = 0.57). Applied to the shock epoch the proposal's own test fails under C1 N1 with all mice (p = 0.054), and citing C2 N1 to keep that part mixes readings, a choice that reaches a result. The control is weak: 5 permutations per mouse, and 5 of 16 mice have a normalised F1 of 0 in every epoch.

paper_notes.statement: The paper's behaviour code and its BehaviorDEPOT cue frames assume 25 frames/s (fps = 25 in batch_PMA_postanalysis_script_BDv15.m, vid_fps 25 in On Plat.mat, 751-frame tone bouts), while in six sessions (F5, M5 and F6 on both days) the camera timestamps give 28.2 to 29.8 frames/s. In those sessions the tone and shock windows drift from the real tones, and the code's success rule disagrees with the hand-scored outcomes on 15 of 60 trials, against 4 with windows placed by the timestamps.

Which frames form a period (from the first tone of the period to the next tone, or from the end of the previous tone to the end of the last), and are D1 and D2 tones 9 to 12 (Results) or the last 3 tones (Methods)? The overall-encoding and tone-proportion claims change outcome between these readings.

Question for the authors: how is a mixed cell counted for Figure 1K to 1M? With the code's category rule (genFeatCellResponses.m) on the Zenodo traces, 24% to 31% of responsive day 2 cells of shocked mice are mixed, against 31% to 34% in non-shocked mice, not 51% against 25%. Did the pie charts use further feature vectors (for example platform stays or the tone and ITI splits) or a different denominator?

Question for the authors: for decoding, which class is positive in the F1 score (the Methods code success as 1, calculatePerformance.m counts failure as positive), and is F1 min-max normalized (Methods) or z-scored (Zscore_Sz in the code)? Shocked mice decode better than non-shocked mice in the pre-shock and shock epochs only with success positive and min-max normalization. The ROC_IDs file that defines the modulated and non-modulated cell sets is not public either.

Question for the authors: which Sidak family were the Figure 1E to 1H block comparisons corrected over, all pairs of blocks or each block against block 1? On the camera-clock tone windows the freezing rise passes only against block 1 (p = 0.047, smallest over all pairs 0.092) and the latency fall only over all pairs (block 2 against 4, p = 0.032).

The notebook links the two, checks the clocks, and tests the behaviour, ROC encoding, platform-event, decoding and Rescorla-Wagner claims.
